newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak NBS leaves repo unchanged but eyeing market.
newsitem.headline: Slovak NBS leaves repo unchanged but eyeing market.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) said on Thursday it had left its repo rate at 9.7 percent after Wednesday's T-bill auction, but added that it could be changed at any time to react to the money market.
"Lately, when necessary, we have reacted immediately after auctions, but this time we decided to wait and watch the market's development," NBS chief dealer Peter Andresic told Reuters.
Preventing banks from arbitraging remained the main possible reason for the NBS to alter its repo rate, he said.

Currency dealers on Wednesday had expected the central bank to change the repo, after average yield at a Finance Ministry 40-week T-bill auction hit 10.12 percent, up from 9.986 percent in the last auction of bills with similar maturity -- 39-week T-bills -- on November 14.
The finance ministry accepted 3.97 billion crowns worth of bids out of total bids of 4.27 billion crowns.
